"JUMBO BUCKS" has had no $2 million top prize claimed for three months. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

The table below shows the full count for "JUMBO BUCKS", with every prize level included.
1639.headline: No new top prize claims

1640.body:
"MEGA BUCKS" has had no $5 million top prize claimed for three weeks. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

How far "MEGA BUCKS" is through its run does not decide anything by itself. It changes how closely to look at the other numbers.

Today's free summary of "MEGA BUCKS" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
1640.headline: Three weeks, no top prize claimed

1641.body:
The most common win left on "POWER 20X" is $5. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and four of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything above about "POWER 20X" comes from the Florida Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
1641.headline: Prize table details

1642.body:
"$500,000 CASH BLITZ" is early in its run, with most of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Every line of $500,000 CASH BLITZ's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
1642.headline: Tickets sold so far

1643.body:
A $9,000 top prize on "WILD 9S" was claimed four days ago. The game started with eighteen top prizes and has fifteen top prizes left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Everything here about "WILD 9S" comes from official Florida lottery numbers, current through October 21.
1643.headline: A top prize was just claimed

1644.body:
"MONEY ROLL" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $50,000 was claimed last week. Unsold tickets still hold five of the original six. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

If you play "MONEY ROLL" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
1644.headline: Another top prize was claimed

1645.body:
On "BLACK PEARLS", one $1 million top prize was claimed two weeks ago. That leaves three of the original four. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

The table below shows the full count for "BLACK PEARLS", with every prize level included.
1645.headline: Fewer $1 million prizes left

1646.body:
Of the unclaimed prize money on "$2,000,000 SPECTACULAR", about three-quarters is in wins under $1,000. The game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

Everything above about "$2,000,000 SPECTACULAR" comes from the Florida Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
1646.headline: The prize mix in this game

1647.body:
Only a small slice of the tickets for "$15,000,000 PLATINUM PAYOUT" have been sold. The game is near the start of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Everything above about "$15,000,000 PLATINUM PAYOUT" comes from the Florida Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.

About two-thirds of the tickets for "20X THE CASH" have been sold. The game is past the halfway point of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

Today's free summary of "20X THE CASH" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
5027.headline: How much has sold

5048.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "FLORIDA 300X THE CASH", only a small slice are still unsold. The game is close to selling out, with one of four top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Each day without a top prize claim on "FLORIDA 300X THE CASH", the remaining top prizes are spread across fewer unsold tickets. The number of tickets printed is fixed.

The numbers for "FLORIDA 300X THE CASH" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
5048.headline: Where this game is in its run

5055.body:
"EMERALD MINE 9X" is close to selling out, with only a small slice of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

If you play "EMERALD MINE 9X" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
5055.headline: Early stage or late

5056.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "JEOPARDY" have been sold. The game is in the second half of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Every line of JEOPARDY's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
5056.headline: Where this game is in its run

5057.body:
"EASY MONEY" has three of eight top prizes left and is well into its run. About three-quarters of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

If "EASY MONEY" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.

About two-thirds of the tickets for "THE CASH WHEEL" are sold. The top prize count has held, with two of six still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

5060.headline: A close look at the prizes

5063.body:
The key fact about "CA$H IN HAND" is how its fourteen prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward the smaller prizes. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.
